script.text: An A.I. agent read private Signal chats in tests. Now Signal is fighting back.

Reuters tested Meta's new A.I. agent, Muse. On an Android phone and on a Mac, it pulled in Signal message text. On an iPhone, it was blocked. Reuters found no sign that Signal's encryption itself was broken.

So how? It simply read what the screen already showed. On the Mac, Reuters reports, it used accessibility features and screenshots. Meta says Muse only reaches data that users allow, and called the reported examples isolated incidents.

Now Signal says it will block screenshots by default on iOS twenty-seven, and on Android when it detects an A.I. assistant. On Macs, it says it cannot do that reliably. Signal's president, Meredith Whittaker, calls the fix incomplete and wants better tools from Apple, Google and Microsoft.
Will Apple, Google and Microsoft let apps lock out A.I. agents? Yes or no?

upload.title: Signal Blocks Screenshots to Keep AI Agents Out #shorts
upload.description:
In a Reuters investigation published November 18, 2026, Meta's AI agent Muse pulled in Signal message text on an Android phone and a Mac and was blocked on an iPhone; Reuters found no sign that Signal's end-to-end encryption was broken. Meta says Muse only reaches data users give it permission to access and called the examples isolated incidents. On November 20, Signal said it will block screenshots by default on iOS 27 and on Android when it detects an AI assistant, says it cannot reliably do so on macOS, and calls the fix incomplete.

Sources: Reuters (via TimesLive, WTVB), Ars Technica (via coverage), The Next Web, Android Authority, Digital Trends, PhoneArena, IBTimes UK, The Hans India.
